about: Fragment selection for the framework workflow. Ground truth is the loading section of step-03, which is where every fragment this workflow reads is named. step-04 gained the write-time enforcement hook in this same change and loads no knowledge fragments, so it is not a context file here; its inputs are the criteria registry and the detected stack, neither of which is a fragment.

cases.name: Scaffolding a mobile test framework
cases.prompt: Set up the test framework for this app. It is a React Native app and we have no tests at all yet.
repoFacts: app.json declares expo; package.json depends on react-native
no tests directory, no .maestro directory yet

assertions.text: mobile-test-strategy.md is marked CRITICAL and load-first because it decides which behaviors become device flows at all, and the step file says most should not. Scaffolding flows without it produces a device suite for work that belonged below the device level.

The three browser fragments are excluded by name: a device flow has no DOM and no request interceptor. This is the same exclusion the automate workflow makes, and the two agreeing is what keeps a scaffolded mobile project from acquiring browser patterns at setup time.

cases.name: Scaffolding a browser framework with playwright-utils enabled
cases.prompt: Set up the test framework for this web app. Nothing exists yet.
repoFacts: package.json depends on react and vite; @seontechnologies/playwright-utils is installed

assertions.text: intercept-network-call.md is added only when the detected stack is frontend or fullstack, on top of the utils set that loads regardless. A backend run with the same flag gets the utils set without it.
The samples this workflow writes are the reference every later workflow copies, so a mandate fragment missing here does not just affect setup: it teaches the wrong pattern permanently.

cases.name: Scaffolding for a Python service with no JavaScript
cases.prompt: Set up the test framework for this FastAPI service. There are no tests yet.
repoFacts: pyproject.toml with FastAPI and httpx; there is no package.json in the repo
no pact artifacts, no browser automation, no .maestro directory

assertions.text: Both library flags default true and a repo with no package.json can have neither package installed, so both mandates stay closed. Scaffolding is the worst place to get this wrong, because a mandate loaded here writes sample files a Python project cannot use.

The Pact relevance gate is a property of the repository, not of tea_use_pactjs_utils. No Pact artifacts, no broker variables, and no separate provider mean nothing Pact-related loads and nothing Pact-related gets scaffolded.
